narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the purpose of the loan, and your credit history. Your checking account balance between 0 and 200 DM was the single biggest reason for the denial. Most approved applicants (59%) have no checking account at all or maintain much healthier balances, so this relatively low balance pushed the prediction noticeably toward higher risk.

Your request to finance a used car worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. Used-car loans are viewed more favorably than many other purposes. Similarly, your past delays in credit repayment also pushed the decision in a positive direction compared with the average approved applicant. However, these two helpful factors were not strong enough to overcome the negative signal from your checking account status.

Given this outcome, you should focus on building a stronger checking account balance and ensuring all future credit payments are made on time. Once your financial profile shows more stability in these areas, reapplying or seeking a smaller loan may improve your chances.
